rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for literal poison and, figuratively, something harmful or corrupting.

example.english: Be careful, this poison can kill people.
example.jyutping: siu2 sam1 ni1 zung2 duk6 wui5 sei2 jan4

rows.note: Use this when the poison is conceived as a drug, dose, or deliberately administered substance rather than poison in general.

example.english: Someone put poison in the tea.
example.traditional: 有人喺杯茶度落咗毒藥。
example.jyutping: jau5 jan4 hai2 bui1 caa4 dou6 lok6 zo2 duk6 joek6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for polluting or contaminating water, land, or other things.

example.english: The factory may poison the river.
example.traditional: 間工廠可能會污染條河。
example.jyutping: gaan1 gung1 cong2 ho2 nang4 wui5 wu1 jim5 tiu4 ho4

rows.note: Use this when someone is killed by being given poison, rather than merely harmed or contaminated.

example.english: Someone used poison to kill the dog.
example.traditional: 有人用毒藥毒死咗隻狗。
example.jyutping: jau5 jan4 jung6 duk6 joek6 duk6 sei2 zo2 zek3 gau2

rows.note: Use this colloquial verb when something causes a situation or relationship to become much worse.

example.english: Doing this will poison the whole situation.
example.traditional: 你咁樣做會搞衰晒成件事喎。
example.jyutping: nei5 gam3 joeng6 zou6 wui5 gaau2 seoi1 saai3 sing4 gin6 si6 wo3

rows.note: Use this when someone causes A to dislike or turn against B, rather than when the issue is physical poisoning.

example.english: His constant bad-mouthing of Ming can poison my feelings toward him.
example.traditional: 佢成日講阿明壞話，搞到我憎阿明。
example.jyutping: keoi5 sing4 jat6 gong2 aa3 ming4 waai6 waa6 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 zang1 aa3 ming4

rows.note: Use this for a person or thing that causes serious harm, especially in a figurative expression such as gossip being a scourge.

example.english: Gossip really is a poison to society.
example.traditional: 流言蜚語真係社會嘅禍害。
example.jyutping: lau4 jin4 fei1 jyu5 zan1 hai6 se5 wui6 ge3 wo6 hoi6
